commit.message:
Make a logged soreness day clickable wherever it is drawn

The journal list had the only way into the editor — a wrench icon beside the
date. Lanes and Timeline draw the same entries and offered hover detail only,
so the view you spot a mistake in was not the view you could fix it in. Since
Lanes is now the landing view, the default page had no edit affordance at all.

A soreness entry is identified by (date, sourceWorkoutId), and both views
already hold that pair for every cell they draw, so each can hand off to the
editor the wrench opens: a lane stripe's logged day, and a filled cell in a
recovery curve. Unlogged days stay inert — there is no entry to edit.

Give kill-me its own devctl environment

devctl will not mark an environment ready until the process on the port proves
it is the exact instance, project, worktree and revision it was asked for, and
kill-me could satisfy neither half of that: no identity endpoint, and Vite's
default host resolves verbatim to ::1 alone here while the probe and the Caddy
route in front of it both dial 127.0.0.1. Every attempt to run this repo under
devctl therefore ended as a failed launch that left an orphaned Vite behind.

So serve /__devctl/health off the DEVCTL_* environment, bind IPv4 loopback, and
honour the assigned port. The endpoint is serve-only and inert unless devctl
launched us, so it cannot reach a production build.

Binding 127.0.0.1 has one consequence worth writing down: headless Chrome does
not fall back from ::1, so a screenshot against localhost now fails silently
with no PNG at all. The verification recipe uses the literal address.
